court: The European Court of Human Rights (Second Section)

holdings.reasoning_summary: The Court found the application met admissibility criteria and was not manifestly ill-founded or inadmissible on other grounds.

holdings.text: Holds, by four votes to three, that there has been a substantive violation of Article 3 of the Convention
holdings.reasoning_summary: The Court concluded that the injuries sustained by the applicant were the result of disproportionate and excessive force by police, violating Article 3's substantive protection against ill-treatment.

holdings.text: Holds unanimously that there has been a procedural violation of Article 3 of the Convention
holdings.reasoning_summary: The Court found serious shortcomings in the investigation into the applicant's ill-treatment allegations, including lack of independence and failure to gather evidence, thus violating procedural obligations under Article 3.

holdings.text: Holds unanimously that there has been a violation of Article 11 of the Convention
holdings.reasoning_summary: The Court held that the police intervention and arrest interfered with the applicant's right to freedom of peaceful assembly and that the interference was disproportionate and unnecessary, violating Article 11.

holdings.text: Holds unanimously that there is no need to examine separately the complaints under Articles 6 and 13 of the Convention
holdings.reasoning_summary: The Court found that no separate issues arose under Articles 6 and 13 given the findings under Articles 3 and 11.

holdings.text: Holds, by four votes to three, that the respondent State is to pay the applicant, within three months of the date on which the judgment becomes final in accordance with Article 44 § 2 of the Convention, EUR 20,000 (twenty thousand euros), plus any tax that may be chargeable, in respect of pecuniary and non-pecuniary damage
holdings.reasoning_summary: The Court awarded just satisfaction for non-pecuniary damage due to the violations found, rejecting pecuniary damage claims as unsubstantiated, and ordered payment with interest.

holdings.text: Dismisses unanimously the remainder of the applicant's claim for just satisfaction

holdings.reasoning_summary: The Court rejected the applicant's claims for costs and expenses due to lack of supporting documentation.

outcome.relief_summary: The Court found substantive and procedural violations of Article 3 and a violation of Article 11. It awarded the applicant EUR 20,000 for non-pecuniary damage and dismissed pecuniary damage and costs claims.
directions: Respondent State to pay EUR 20,000 to applicant within three months plus default interest thereafter
